label: 3-day, 10-year storm, change
description: Change in rain in the 3-day, 10-year storm: multi-day rain that comes about once a decade
details: NOAA Atlas 14 (model’s 1979–2005) → 2050–2079 · mean of GFDL-CM3 and NCAR-CCSM4 · RCP 8.5
method: Percent change in the 3-day, 10-year storm: 100 × (2050–2079 depth ÷ NOAA Atlas 14 depth − 1). The 2050–2079 depth is the mean of SNAP's DOT precipitation-frequency projections for GFDL-CM3 and NCAR-CCSM4 (WRF-downscaled, RCP 8.5; local netCDFs pcpt_<model>_sum_wrf_3d_2050-2079.nc, interval 10), ~480 m cells averaged to the 1 km grid. Atlas 14 is Volume 7 (Alaska), annual maximum series (hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pub/hdsc/data/ak/ak10yr03da_ams.zip, 1/1000 inch, NAD83 lon/lat), averaged over 3 × 3 points per 1 km cell. SNAP's DOT depths are Atlas 14 × each model's change since 1979–2005 (Bieniek et al. 2022; SNAP's pipeline uses the annual maximum series), so this is the models' projected change since 1979–2005.
pros: Multi-day rain that comes about once a decade: repeated slope saturation and high water
Both models project an increase on 94 % of land (but they split on direction in 14 % of the South)
Estimated from more events than the 100-year storm, so less noisy
cons: The two models don't agree on where the change is largest (rank correlation near 0); the average's pattern mostly follows GFDL-CM3, which projects about twice the change of NCAR-CCSM4
Smaller changes in a narrow range: median +31 %, middle 90 % of land +11 to +52 %
sources: SNAP DOT precipitation frequency, local netCDFs (3d, 2050–2079, interval 10, both models)
author: Joshdpaul
